chapters.title: Human Nature and the Heroic
chapters.sourcePressure: Introduces heroism as a basic human motive tied to narcissism, modern disillusion, and the need for vital concepts.
chapters.coreMove: read heroism as the ordinary need to matter, not as rare public greatness
chapters.commonMisread: Heroism just means confidence, ambition, or inspirational courage.

chapters.title: The Terror of Death
chapters.sourcePressure: Treats fear of death as universal, impossible to hold constantly in consciousness, and often managed through repression and coping patterns.
chapters.coreMove: notice how repressed death terror gets displaced into ordinary control, routines, and symbolic safety
chapters.commonMisread: Fear of death is only a conscious phobia or occasional gloomy thought.

chapters.title: The Recasting of Some Basic Psychoanalytic Ideas
chapters.sourcePressure: Recasts psychoanalytic ideas around creatureliness, body shame, repression, and embodied finitude rather than sexuality alone.
chapters.coreMove: see the human split between symbolic self and finite body as the source of shame and defense
chapters.commonMisread: The problem is body image or embarrassment in a narrow modern sense.

chapters.title: Human Character as a Vital Lie
chapters.sourcePressure: Defines character as organized defense and the vital lie as protective and distorting at once.
chapters.coreMove: treat character as a necessary narrowing of reality that stabilizes identity while hiding unbearable truths
chapters.commonMisread: Character is merely personality type or moral strength.

chapters.title: The Psychoanalyst Kierkegaard
chapters.sourcePressure: Turns to Kierkegaard as a deeper psychologist of anxiety, inwardness, dependence, finitude, and meaning.
chapters.coreMove: read anxiety and despair as problems of selfhood before dependence and finitude, not merely symptoms to suppress
chapters.commonMisread: The point is simply to be spiritual or to stop overthinking.

chapters.title: The Problem of Freud's Character, Noch Einmal
chapters.sourcePressure: Revisits Freud as a major psychological force whose own character narrowed parts of his theory.
chapters.coreMove: hold admiration and critique together by seeing how a thinker's character can shape both insight and blindness
chapters.commonMisread: The chapter is either a takedown of Freud or a defense of Freud.

chapters.title: The Spell Cast by Persons: The Nexus of Unfreedom
chapters.sourcePressure: Explains transference, dependency, and submission to powerful persons as terror management through borrowed certainty.
chapters.coreMove: identify when another person becomes a borrowed source of reality, worth, and safety
chapters.commonMisread: Dependency is only gullibility or weakness.

chapters.title: Otto Rank and the Closure of Psychoanalysis on Kierkegaard
chapters.sourcePressure: Uses Otto Rank to widen psychology toward love, creativity, religion, and the burden placed on partial answers.
chapters.coreMove: separate real transcendence hunger from the fragile finite forms that people ask to satisfy it totally
chapters.commonMisread: Love, art, or faith automatically solves mortality anxiety.

chapters.title: The Present Outcome of Psychoanalysis
chapters.sourcePressure: Judges psychoanalysis as insightful about repression and conflict but insufficient as a cure because it lacks a strong world-picture.
chapters.coreMove: see insight without a convincing world-picture as diagnosis that may expose defense without healing failed heroism
chapters.commonMisread: More self insight is automatically enough.

chapters.title: A General View of Mental Illness
chapters.sourcePressure: Offers a historically situated general view of mental illness as distorted death-transcendence while preserving continuity with ordinary defense.
chapters.coreMove: read mental breakdown as an extreme, reality-breaking version of the same human search for heroism and protection
chapters.commonMisread: Mental illness is just a metaphor for existential struggle.

chapters.title: Psychology and Religion: What Is the Heroic Individual?
chapters.sourcePressure: Closes with psychology and religion as a final tension around courage, humility, limitation, transcendence, and the heroic individual.
chapters.coreMove: choose a humbler heroism that faces limitation without pretending psychology or religion offers a neat escape
chapters.commonMisread: The ending offers a simple cure for death anxiety.
